edits.new: The north-zone distribution system currently holds a minimum pressure of 42 psi [BASTION]. The restoration gate requires at least 35 psi at every critical node for three consecutive thirty-minute windows; the current 42 psi reading does not by itself satisfy this multi-window requirement, and psi values must not be converted to kPa or treated as proof of water quality [BASTION]. Ridge storage contains 5.8 million gallons, while the twelve-hour emergency reserve is 3.2 million gallons; these are distinct measures and must not be conflated as treated reserve [BASTION]. DELTA pump sequencing depends on BASTION pressure and ECHO power; cavitation constraints limit shared-main capacity under staged demand conditions [DELTA, BASTION, ECHO]. Pressure warnings at 38 psi and isolation triggers at 30 psi are distinct control states: a warning does not initiate isolation, and an isolation trigger does not merely warn [INDIGO, BASTION]. Residence time in the distribution loop must be verified against candidate-bound hydraulic model H12; any change to valve map V8 or controller firmware C11 invalidates prior residence-time evidence [MOSAIC]. The current minimum pressure of 42 psi exceeds the 30 psi isolation trigger but remains within the operational band defined by H12; no isolation action is currently indicated, though the three-consecutive-window restoration gate must still be met before hydraulic clearance can be claimed [BASTION, INDIGO].

edits.new: Clearance requires two complete sampling rounds spaced at least sixteen hours apart; one clean round is insufficient. The current confirmatory set comprises forty-eight samples with zero E. coli positives across all locations [CIPHER].
edits.old: Clearance requires two complete sampling rounds spaced at least sixteen hours apart; one clean round is insufficient [CIPHER].

edits.new: Emergency generation can carry 4.1 MW for thirty-six hours at the current fuel stock; the duration is not thirty-six days and excludes mobile-pump load [ECHO]. The grid feed is rated at 8.2 MW, but the damaged switchgear limits current delivery to 6.5 MW; rated power is not usable power [ECHO]. KESTREL diesel stock covers emergency load for 36 hours and full pump load for 22 hours; these load regimes are distinct and must not be merged as a single duration [KESTREL, ECHO]. Coagulant and chlorine chemical stocks provide 4.5 days and 3.2 days of treatment capacity respectively; inventory duration is not delivery lead time [KESTREL, FALCON]. Staffing continuity depends on mutual-aid logistics; current shift coverage must be verified against the 36-hour generator window [KESTREL]. Any change to ECHO power state or KESTREL fuel stock makes prior pump sequencing evidence stale [DELTA, ECHO, KESTREL]. The shared transmission main is capped at 14.5 million gallons per day, and pump nameplate capacities cannot be summed into usable system flow; the latest inspected configuration sustained 12.8 MGD after fire-flow and hospital reserve [DELTA]. Restoration may advance through ten, thirty, sixty, and one hundred percent demand stages only after two consecutive thirty-minute windows meet pressure, turbidity, power, and storage gates [DELTA]. The shared-main limit under staged demand requires that DELTA pump capacity not exceed the 6.5 MW usable grid feed plus any available generator margin without triggering cavitation constraints [DELTA, ECHO, BASTION].

Any change to ECHO power state or KESTREL fuel stock makes prior pump sequencing evidence stale [DELTA, ECHO, KESTREL]. edits.new: Critical-signal telemetry coverage stands at 96 percent, with 4 percent of monitored points unobserved; this coverage gap does not prove the uninstrumented zones are healthy, only that they are not currently observable [INDIGO]. Telemetry delay is 700 milliseconds at p95 and 1,200 milliseconds at p99; both are observations, not control deadlines [INDIGO]. Pressure warnings at 38 psi and isolation triggers at 30 psi are distinct control states; a warning does not initiate isolation, and an isolation trigger does not merely warn [INDIGO, BASTION]. Telemetry delays in the unobserved 4 percent create uncertainty that must be treated as potential adverse condition until verified by direct observation or alternate telemetry [INDIGO]. Warnings versus actions: a pressure warning at 38 psi requires monitoring and logging but does not require isolation; an isolation trigger at 30 psi requires immediate valve closure and zone separation [INDIGO, BASTION]. Any change to hydraulic model H12, pump plan P9, or control-system key set W4 invalidates prior telemetry correlation evidence and requires re-verification of coverage and alert thresholds [MOSAIC, INDIGO, BASTION, DELTA, ECHO, FALCON]. Alternate telemetry paths must be identified for the 4 percent unobserved zone before closure can be claimed [INDIGO, NEXUS].
